evidence.claim: The Defence Ministry said a routine-maintenance technical malfunction caused an accidental missile firing into Pakistan and ordered a high-level Court of Inquiry.
evidence.title: Statement on accidental firing of missile
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Defence Ministry said a routine-maintenance technical malfunction caused an accidental missile firing into Pakistan and ordered a high-level Court of Inquiry.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government statement released the day after the incident.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and squarely on the ruler-period safety question.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government action under Modi's executive authority; the statement reflects institutional response, not a personal order.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not identify a specific launcher or command-chain breakdown, so it is not proof of personal negligence or intent.

evidence.claim: Reuters reporting said the accidental launch raised questions about safety mechanisms and could have endangered passenger flights and civilians.
evidence.title: India says it accidentally fired missile into Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reporting said the accidental launch raised questions about safety mechanisms and could have endangered passenger flights and civilians.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs of the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced contemporaneous reporting adds independent corroboration to the official admission.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the same incident as the official statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the consequences of the Indian state apparatus under Modi's tenure, not a direct ruler order.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes that the missile was unarmed and that the incident was framed as accidental, so it does not by itself show deliberate escalation.

evidence.claim: Modi said he had appealed to both Putin and Zelenskyy for peace, condemned the Bucha killings, said India had sent medicines and relief materials to Ukraine and neighbouring countries, and urged direct talks.
evidence.title: English Translation of Remarks by Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi at virtual meeting with the President of the USA
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: Modi said he had appealed to both Putin and Zelenskyy for peace, condemned the Bucha killings, said India had sent medicines and relief materials to Ukraine and neighbouring countries, and urged direct talks.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs beginning 'The news of the recent killings...' and 'We have sent medicines and other relief materials...'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government transcription/translation of the PM’s remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler statement, though still self-reported diplomacy.
contrary_evidence: The source is an official translation and a self-presentation of policy, so it should be triangulated with UN records and other diplomatic readouts.

evidence.claim: Modi expressed deep concern at the mounting humanitarian crisis in Ukraine and reiterated his call for an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy.
evidence.title: Visit of the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom to India (April 21-22, 2022)
evidence.excerpt: Modi expressed deep concern at the mounting humanitarian crisis in Ukraine and reiterated his call for an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO record of a dated bilateral statement.
contrary_evidence: This is a diplomatic statement with no direct enforcement mechanism, so it shows posture more than measurable outcome.

evidence.claim: Modi called for an early cessation of hostilities, said there can be no military solution, and emphasized the importance of respecting the UN Charter and the safety of nuclear installations in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Telephone Conversation between Prime Minister and President of Ukraine
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: Modi called for an early cessation of hostilities, said there can be no military solution, and emphasized the importance of respecting the UN Charter and the safety of nuclear installations in Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO/PIB release with a dated direct conversation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler statement and diplomatic action.
contrary_evidence: The nuclear-installation point is relevant to catastrophic-risk avoidance, but the call still did not produce a settlement or verified de-escalation on the ground.

evidence.claim: The two sides said dialogue through military and diplomatic channels should continue until a mutually acceptable resolution is reached, and that this would help restore peace and tranquility along the LAC.
evidence.title: Joint Release of the 15th Round of China-India Corps Commander Level Meeting
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The two sides said dialogue through military and diplomatic channels should continue until a mutually acceptable resolution is reached, and that this would help restore peace and tranquility along the LAC.
evidence.source_locator: body text of the joint release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government release on the border talks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional border-policy posture under Modi’s government.
contrary_evidence: The release confirms continuing friction, so it is evidence of de-escalation management rather than a final peaceful settlement.
